rules.quoted_span: Increase in residential rents are limited to the lower of 3% per year, or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period.
rules.interaction: Local rent stabilization; the state AB 1482 cap yields to it where it is stricter.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property in Santa Ana
rules.exemptions: residential buildings constructed after February 1, 1995; mobile home spaces offered for rent after January 1, 1990
rules.key_value: lower of 3% or 80% of CPI change
rules.title: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization Ordinance
rules.requirement: Rent increases are limited to the lower of 3% per year or 80% of the 12-month CPI change; no increase if CPI is negative. Owners may petition for a higher increase to ensure a fair return.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance (Rent Stabilization Program)

rules.quoted_span: Under a no-fault just cause termination, the owner shall either provide 3 months of relocation assistance or waive payment of rent for the final 3 months of the tenancy.

any.unavailable: deed-restricted affordable housing, hotel, care facility, dormitory or shared living quarters

rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property in Santa Ana, after the first 30 days of tenancy
rules.exemptions: housing produced in the last 15 years; deed-restricted affordable housing; hotel and transient occupancy; hospital and care facilities; dormitories; other shared living quarters
rules.key_value: 3 months' relocation assistance or rent waiver for no-fault terminations
rules.title: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.requirement: After 30 days an owner may not end a tenancy without just cause stated in a written notice, after first giving notice and time to cure; for no-fault causes the owner pays 3 months of relocation assistance or waives the last 3 months of rent.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance (Rent Stabilization Program)

notes: City press release on the 2021 adoption; both ordinances effective 2021-11-19 (text says effective Nov 19 and 'not effective until November 19, 2021'). No ordinance number or code cite is given. Rent cap numbers are the adopted 2021 terms; later changes (e.g. the 2.87% annual rate) are in D084.
